units.title: Body Iron & Daily Needs
units.sec: Body Iron Pools and Daily Requirements
units.guide:
Male 50 mg/kg; female 40 mg/kg. Pools: Hb 67%, storage 27%, transferrin 0.08%, myoglobin 3.5%, labile 2.2%.
Prussian blue is the marrow-store gold standard; hemosiderin + ferrocyanide turns blue-black.
Daily requirements and p70 Hb thresholds are included as printed.

units.title: Dietary Iron & Absorption
units.guide:
Heme Fe²⁺/HCP versus non-heme Fe³⁺/duodenal cytochrome b reductase → Fe²⁺/DMT1.
Reducing substances and acidic pH enhance absorption; phytate, tannate and oxalate inhibit it.
The diagram follows mucosal storage, epithelial shedding and basolateral export.

units.title: Export, Transport & Marrow Uptake
units.sec: Iron Export, Transport and Marrow Uptake
units.guide:
Ferroportin exports iron; liver hepcidin inhibits it; hephaestin oxidizes Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺ for transferrin.
Marrow TfR1/TfR2 → acidic endosome → Fe²⁺/DMT1 → common iron pool → mitochondrial heme.
A source-note direction for ceruloplasmin is flagged as printed and should be verified before clinical use.

units.title: Serum Iron Indices
units.guide:
Ferritin 30–300 ng/mL; serum iron 50–150 µg/dL; TIBC 300–360 µg/dL; TSAT 33%.
Iron deficiency: ferritin/iron/TSAT low and TIBC/sTfR high; ferritin can be masked by acute-phase response.
Low ferritin is earliest; sTfR is most sensitive; sTfR/log ferritin is listed as most specific.

units.title: Stages of Iron Deficiency
units.guide:
Stage I: pre-latent/negative balance; Stage II: latent/iron-deficient erythropoiesis; Stage III: IDA.
TSAT falls below 20% then 15%; TIBC, sTfR and FEP rise; reticulocyte Hb falls from Stage II.
Stage II remains normocytic/normochromic; Stage III has anaemia, microcytosis/hypochromia and pica/epithelial changes.

units.title: Causes & Iron Deficit
units.guide:
Blood loss is emphasized ('unless proven otherwise'); menstruation and haemorrhoids are listed.
Malabsorption: celiac (duodenum), tropical sprue (pan-intestinal); CKD and nutrition are also listed.
The 2.3 × Hb-difference × weight + 1000 mg formula and EPO-after-iron note are transcribed.

units.title: Clinical Features
units.guide:
Oral lesions: angular cheilitis/stomatitis, candidiasis, median rhomboid and atrophic glossitis.
Plummer–Vinson: dysphagia + oesophageal webs; other findings include koilonychia, pagophagia and hair loss.
Growth/development, splenomegaly, heart failure and neuropsychiatric features are also inventoried.

units.title: IDA Investigations
units.guide:
Ferritin, serum iron, TSAT fall; TIBC, sTfR, red-cell protoporphyrin and RDW rise.
MCH 27–31 pg; Mentzer >13 favors IDA, <13 thalassaemia trait; smear shows anisopoikilocytosis.
Tear-drop cells, hypochromia, pencil cells and microcytes are labelled in the figures.

units.title: Marrow, Treatment & Follow-up
units.guide:
Marrow: absent Prussian-blue stores and erythroid hyperplasia.
The page lists parenteral iron for Stage III, oral iron for latent disease and gastric intolerance.
Reticulocytes rise at 5–7 days/peak 10–14; Hb starts at two weeks; dosing is reproduced as printed, not current guidance.
